Needs changes before merge.

Safety-tier review. The PR adds geometry and an NC program. It does not change the machining algorithms.

**Requested before merge**

1. `crates/app/tests/example_catalog_adaptive.rs:10`: Register the new case in `crates/app/tests/example_catalog.rs` with both named catalog tests. Current main requires `catalog_2d_adaptive_pocket::regenerates` and `catalog_2d_adaptive_pocket::rebuilds`. Each must call the existing `run_case` helper with the corresponding action. The new parameter test runs in a separate executable. It does not supply these registrations. After the trial merge, `contract::every_case_has_two_named_test_results` fails. The normal catalog suite also does not regenerate or rebuild this case. Keep the new parameter test as additional coverage.

Exact failure:

```text
missing case test catalog_2d_adaptive_pocket::regenerates: test

test result: FAILED. 15 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

**Local build and tests**

Trial merge with upstream main `acd5b02d3e36a12745b11038012240781129d43c`: clean. The checks used this merged tree and the laws from current upstream main.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: build passed; `example_catalog` had 15 passes and 1 failure; `example_catalog_adaptive` passed its one test.
- `cargo xtask catalog --check`: all seven cases passed. The script rebuilt and verified the new case. Its NC output matched the committed program byte for byte.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --only 'app heavy: example_catalog'`: succeeded in release mode. It ran zero tests, with 16 filtered out. This gives no additional heavy-test coverage.

**Extra suites run**

The changed catalog directory is fixture data. I checked its readers and ran both suites that discover the new case:

- App `example_catalog`: 15 passed, 1 failed, as reported above. The quick gate ran this whole suite.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --test catalog_render`, from `crates/ui`: 1 passed, 1 ignored. The ignored test renders catalog screenshots.

The other catalog tests read different case directories or temporary fixtures. No importer code or STEP fixture changed. The extra kernel STEP suites do not apply.

**Mutations re-run**

- Change the saved Adaptive wall allowance from 0.5 to 0: the new pin failed at the wall-allowance assertion. Restore the original bytes: passed.
- Change the saved Adaptive bottom from Z6.5 to Z6: the new pin failed at the floor-allowance assertion. Restore the original bytes: passed.

Both mutations changed only the review copy. The original fixture bytes were restored after each check.

**Golden and scope checks**

The new NC golden has 13,325 lines. I checked all lines for motion values, depths, wall clearance, and rapid-move direction. I checked the radii and swept wall clearance of all 3,694 arcs. Roughing reaches Z6.5; finishing reaches Z6. The tool, operation order, allowance limits, and retracts agree with the case description. The rebuild check also compared every NC byte. No existing NC golden changed.

The model is embedded. The README states the corner stock and verification limits. No UI source changed, so before/after UI screenshots are not required. No physical machine test was run.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: Register the Adaptive pocket case in the normal catalog suite.

- Added `catalog_2d_adaptive_pocket::regenerates` and `catalog_2d_adaptive_pocket::rebuilds`. Both call `run_case` with the corresponding action. Both tests pass. The separate parameter test remains unchanged and passes.
- The existing `contract::every_case_has_two_named_test_results` pins both registrations. Removing each registration separately gives RED with its missing name. Restoring each gives GREEN with an isolated catalog. The unchanged contract also passes when only the unrelated upstream groove fixture is excluded. All source and fixture bytes were restored.
- Merged `upstream/main` cleanly to use the current catalog helper and contract.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: RED. The catalog suite has 17 passes and one failure: `missing case test catalog_turning_groove_part_off::regenerates: test`. This separate upstream registration is outside the requested fix. Both adaptive tests pass in the full suite.

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN.

New head: `140a289e10852a143bc0157d2c48f0276a1f6b0a`.

Please re-review this head.

Needs changes before merge: the full catalog suite remains red.

Safety-tier review. This PR adds geometry and an NC program.

**Earlier finding**

The Adaptive registration finding is resolved. Both named tests call `run_case` with the correct action. Both pass. The separate parameter test also passes. I found no new defect in the Adaptive case.

**Required before readiness**

1. `crates/app/tests/example_catalog/contract.rs:23`: Restore a green full catalog suite after the upstream groove/part-off registration is fixed. Then run the quick gate against that main. The suite cannot find `catalog_turning_groove_part_off::regenerates`. The registration contract requires both actions. This is an upstream defect, not a defect introduced by this PR. I reproduced the same failure on exact upstream main `acd5b02d3e36a12745b11038012240781129d43c`. The review instructions treat suite failures as blockers. I therefore retain `needs-rework` until this prerequisite is met. The upstream fix can remain separate from this PR.

```text
missing case test catalog_turning_groove_part_off::regenerates: test

test result: FAILED. 17 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out
```

**Local build and tests**

The review used `.claude/worktrees/review-2963`. Trial merge with upstream main `acd5b02d3e36a12745b11038012240781129d43c` was clean: the PR already contains it. I read the laws from that upstream main. No GitHub runner was used.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: build passed. `example_catalog` had 17 passes and the one failure above. `example_catalog_adaptive` passed its one test.
- `cargo xtask catalog --check`: all seven cases passed. The new script rebuilt and verified the case. Every NC byte matched the committed program.
- `cargo clippy -j 16 -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --only 'app heavy: example_catalog'`: succeeded in release mode. It ran zero tests, with 18 filtered out. This supplies no heavy-test coverage.
- Baseline check on exact upstream main: `cargo test -j 16 -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog contract::every_case_has_two_named_test_results -- --exact` failed with the same missing groove/part-off name. I restored the PR checkout after this check.

**Extra suites run**

I searched the test sources for readers of the changed catalog directory. The full app `example_catalog` suite ran in the quick gate. The new `example_catalog_adaptive` suite also ran there. `cargo test -j 16 -p camcraft-ui --test catalog_render`, from `crates/ui`, passed: 1 passed, 1 ignored. The ignored test renders screenshots. Other catalog tests read different case directories. No importer code or STEP fixture changed, so the extra kernel STEP suites do not apply.

**Mutations re-run**

- Saved Adaptive wall allowance, 0.5 to 0: RED at the wall-allowance assertion. Restore the original bytes: GREEN.
- Saved Adaptive bottom, Z6.5 to Z6: RED at the floor-allowance assertion. Restore the original bytes: GREEN.

Both mutations used the review copy. All fixture bytes were restored.

**Golden and scope checks**

I checked all 13,325 NC lines with an independent parser. It checked finite motion values, feeds, depths, rapid moves, arc radii, and swept wall clearance. All 3,694 arcs passed. The largest radius discrepancy was 0.001251 mm. Roughing reaches Z6.5 with 0.5 mm wall stock. Finishing reaches Z6 with zero wall stock. I inspected both operation transitions and the two Z9 rapid re-entries. Each re-entry returns vertically to a location cut on the previous level. XY rapid moves remain above the stock. The rebuild tests also compare every NC byte. No existing NC golden changed.

The model is embedded. The README states the remaining corner stock and verification limits. No UI source changed, so before/after screenshots are not required. No physical machine test was run.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
